verdict.summary: Total prompt ~146 tok < 512 minimum — nothing will cache. Expanding the static content to reach the floor is often worthwhile.

enablement.detail: OPT-IN: nothing caches unless you mark a breakpoint with "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"} (<= 4 breakpoints; 20-block lookback). Render order is tools -> system -> messages; a byte change invalidates everything after it.
enablement.action: Add "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"} on the LAST static block (end of system prompt or last stable message). For >5-min gaps use {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"} (2x write premium).

provider_intel.ttl: 5 min (refreshed FREE on every hit) / 1h opt-in via ttl:'1h'
provider_intel.write_cost: write premium: 1.25x (5-min TTL) / 2x (1-hour TTL); no storage fee
provider_intel.batch: STACKS with the Batch API 50%: cache read in a batch = 0.1x * 0.5x = ~95% off
gotchas: Below the model's minimum the marked prefix SILENTLY won't cache (cache_creation_input_tokens: 0, no error).
Model switch = cold cache (model-scoped). Toggling extended thinking invalidates system+messages (tools survive).
Serialize tool JSON deterministically (sorted keys, frozen order) — non-deterministic serialization is a classic silent invalidator.
Concurrency: entry readable only after the first response begins streaming — warm one, then fan out.
Pre-warm with a max_tokens: 0 request to skip cold-write latency on the first real request.
On Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5: append {"role": "system", ...} to messages for mid-conversation instructions instead of editing the top-level system prompt — preserves the cached prefix.
No prompt_cache_key equivalent — routing affinity cannot be steered; identical prefixes are the only lever.

recommendations: [enablement] Add "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"} on the LAST static block (end of system prompt or last stable message). For >5-min gaps use {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"} (2x write premium).

[verify] After deploying, assert usage.cache_read_input_tokens (writes: usage.cache_creation_input_tokens) > 0 in responses. 0 across identical-prefix requests = a silent invalidator is still present.
[batch] STACKS with the Batch API 50%: cache read in a batch = 0.1x * 0.5x = ~95% off
warnings: 1 non-text block(s) (images/documents) approximated as placeholders — token counts underestimate them.
Token counts are estimates (estimate(~3.5 chars/tok)). for exact counts use POST /v1/messages/count_tokens (never tiktoken for Claude)

meta.caveat: Thresholds/prices are time-sensitive; verify against live provider docs.

threshold.tier: uniform for all OpenAI models (+128-token steps)

verdict.summary: Total prompt ~5 tok < 1024 minimum — nothing will cache. Expanding the static content to reach the floor is often worthwhile.

enablement.detail: Caching is on by default for prompts >= 1,024 tokens — no request changes needed. Reuse the exact prefix; cached amounts grow in 128-token steps.

provider_intel.ttl: 5-10 min sliding; up to 24h extended retention (non-ZDR default since May 2026)
provider_intel.read_discount: per-model 50% -> 98.75% (90% on GPT-5.x) — NOT a flat 50%
provider_intel.write_cost: free through GPT-5.5; ~1.25x input on GPT-5.6+ (single-use large prompts pay the premium for nothing)
provider_intel.routing: prompt_cache_key — same string per prefix-group; keep <= ~15 RPM per key
provider_intel.batch: batch x caching stacking is UNDOCUMENTED (open question in the research)
gotchas: A cache entry becomes readable only after the writing request completes — N simultaneous cold requests all pay full price. Warm one, then fan out.
Discount is per-model; verify against the live pricing page before quoting numbers.
